---
title: "From FASTQ to Outbreak"
subtitle: "Genomic surveillance training — African STARS Fellowship · CARE · Institut Pasteur"
---

This site gathers the whole hands-on course, from raw sequencing reads to an outbreak brief.
Everything runs on a **synthetic** toy virus (`TOYV1`, 10 kb): no real patient data, nothing sensitive.

## The learning path

| # | Module | You will learn to… |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | [FASTQ → consensus genome](course/01-concepts.qmd) | read FASTQ files, do QC, map reads, inspect coverage, build a consensus and decide if it is usable |
| 2 | [Alignment, lineage & reference selection](course/02-reference-selection.qmd) | choose a reference, align genomes, assign a lineage |
| 3 | [Build and read a phylogenetic tree](course/03-build-tree.qmd) | infer a tree, root it, read clades, support and branch lengths |
| 4 | [Communicating genomic evidence](course/04-evidence.qmd) | turn results into clear, honest statements for decision makers |
| 5 | [Mini outbreak investigation](course/05-scenario.qmd) | put everything together on a three-region outbreak |

Module 1 is the 3-hour bridge session (talk + dry lab); modules 2–3 are Day 4 (phylogenetics) and modules 4–5 are Day 5 (capstone).

## How to work

1. Do the [setup](exercises/00_setup.md) once.
2. Follow the pages in the order of the left menu; each exercise ends with a question to discuss.
3. If a tool will not install, use the **plan B** files in `precomputed/` (each page tells you when).
4. Fill in your answer sheet and, on Day 5, your one-page brief.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Data at a glance
Five sequencing samples (S01–S05) for module 1, 27 outbreak genomes (OB01–OB27) for modules 2–5.
All files are in the [repository](https://github.com/YOUR-ORG/fastq-to-genome) under `data/`.
:::
